1.why: Text is set in a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing and generous vertical gaps between form groups, though letter spacing appears default rather than explicitly widened.

2.why: All instructions appear in short sentence-case strings with no italics, no all-caps text, and no dense paragraphs on any screen.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single-column card with large text and full-width buttons that reads well and should fit a phone screen, although I only observed it at one viewport width.

4.why: Instructions are brief plain-language sentences such as 'Sign in to begin. Take your time.' and 'Enter the same contact details again.'

5.why: Placeholders like 'name@example.com' and '07123 456789' plus 'Demo:' hints show exactly what the expected input should look like.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than a couple of short sentences before acting.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard affordance appears on any screen, the phone number had to be re-typed by hand at step 2, and the flow crashed before any code was ever issued in copyable form.

8.why: No QR code is offered anywhere; the provisioning attempt produced the 'Invalid array length' error instead of a QR-or-manual-entry choice.

9.why: The email, phone, and password fields look like standard labelled HTML inputs that autofill could plausibly fill, but the screenshots neither confirm autocomplete support nor show it being blocked.

10.why: A 'Step X of 6 · <name>' header plus one large blue button make the current step and primary action obvious on every screen, including during the error state.

11.why: Each screen requests exactly one main action via a single primary button ('Sign in and continue' / 'Confirm my identity').

12.why: After sign-in the banner plainly says 'You are signed in. Next, confirm your identity.', but after confirming identity the only feedback is the cryptic 'Invalid array length', so not every action is followed by a plain statement of what happened and what comes next.

13.why: Hints explicitly state 'No reading timer. You can retry any step' and 'You can correct and retry these details' and the user could re-submit without lockout, though reveal/hide/re-request of codes was unreachable because the flow broke.

14.why: The only error message observed is the raw technical exception 'Invalid array length', which states neither the problem nor the fix.

15.why: The interface explicitly promises 'No reading timer' and no countdown or deadline appears on any screen, though generous code-entry time could not be directly verified because the flow never reached code entry.
